exercises.name: Ab crunch machine
cues: Adjust the seat and pads to fit you, sit down and grip the handles.
Curl your torso forward by contracting your abs, not by pulling with your arms.
Return slowly under control.
exercises.safety: Slow and controlled; no swinging or momentum.

exercises.name: Ab wheel roll-out (kneeling)
cues: Kneel with your hands on the wheel directly in front of your knees.
Brace and roll forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to head, back flat.
Pull back to the start with your abs.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight; if your lower back sags, roll out less far. The straight-leg version is for experienced trainees only.

exercises.name: Alternating dumbbell curl
cues: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides, palms facing forward, elbows close to your body.
Curl one dumbbell up by bending the elbow.
Lower it to the start, then curl the other. One rep = both arms.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight.

exercises.name: Arnold press
cues: Sit upright with back support. Start with the dumbbells in front of your chest, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating your palms to face forward.
Finish with straight arms over your shoulders.
Lower while rotating back to palms facing you.
exercises.safety: Use lighter weights than your normal dumbbell press; the rotation makes it harder.

exercises.name: Back extension (45°)
cues: Set the top pad against the top of your thighs, feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Cross your arms on your chest (or hold a plate there for more load).
Lower your upper body slowly over the pad.
Raise until your body is in a straight line, squeeze your glutes, pause, and lower slowly. Don't arch past straight.
exercises.safety: Slow, no swinging. You should feel a pump in your lower back and glutes, not a deep ache; if it aches, take a week or two off and come back lighter.

exercises.name: Band chest fly (standing)
cues: Anchor a band at chest height behind you. Hold the ends, step forward until you feel tension, chest up, feet about shoulder-width, core braced.
With a slight, fixed elbow bend, bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Return slowly to the start; shoulders down and back, the rest of your body still.
exercises.safety: Move slowly: fast reps make the band wobble. Heavy bands with low reps aren't recommended. The reference does one arm at a time; both together, each arm moves the same way.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Standing resistance band chest fly

exercises.name: Band lateral walk
cues: Put a band around your ankles.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward a little at the hips.
Walk sideways, so each step brings your leg out against the band. Then walk back the other way.
Count steps per leg.
exercises.safety: Pick a band that's neither too easy nor too hard to stretch.

exercises.name: Band pull-apart
cues: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight, hands about shoulder-width.
Pull the band apart by moving your arms out to the sides until they point straight out.
Return to the start with control.
exercises.safety: Adjust the difficulty with your grip width (narrower is harder) or a stronger band. Check the band for nicks.

exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
cues: Throw the band over the bar and pull one end through the other. A thicker band gives more help.
Step up on a bench or box beside the bar and put your foot in the loop. Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, palms away.
Chest up, look at the bar, and pull until your chin is over the bar or the bar touches your upper chest.
Lower with control until your arms are fully extended.
exercises.safety: Setting up is the tricky part: step into and out of the band carefully, holding the bar. The band helps most at the bottom and least at the top. Move to thinner bands as you get stronger.

exercises.name: Bar dip
cues: Grip the bars about shoulder-width apart and climb or jump into the top position. Knees slightly bent, ankles crossed.
Keep your shoulders down and back; your elbows go backward, not out.
Lower with control until your shoulders are just below your elbows, or as deep as you comfortably can.
Push back up to the start without shrugging toward your ears.
exercises.safety: Dips are stressful on the shoulders and sternum: start with low volume, build it and your depth gradually over the first weeks, and stop if your shoulders hurt (a bench press works the same muscles). A band under your feet or knees makes it lighter; hang weight from a belt to make it harder.

exercises.name: Barbell back squat
cues: Set the bar at about sternum height. Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, bar on your upper back; unrack and take three steps back.
Take a comfortable stance (narrow to wide all work), toes slightly out. Breathe in and brace.
Squat down by bending your knees, hips and ankles, back straight, until your thighs are below parallel or you reach your natural depth limit.
Drive back up to standing. Re-rack by walking in and squatting the bar down onto the hooks.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique. Always set the safety arms just below your lowest point. Wear firm shoes; a raised heel (lifting shoes) helps many people, but don't stand on plates.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
cues: Eyes under the bar, feet planted, glutes and upper back on the bench. Pull your shoulder blades back and down and keep them there.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders, thumbs around the bar, bar low in the palm over your wrists.
Lower with control until the bar touches your chest around the sternum, elbows about 45° from your sides. Don't bounce it.
Press up and slightly back toward your face until your arms are straight.
exercises.safety: Set the safety arms just below chest height or use a spotter, and keep your thumbs wrapped around the bar. Don't push your hips off the bench.

exercises.name: Barbell curl
cues: Stand tall, feet hip-width, core braced. Grip the bar underhand about shoulder-width.
Curl the bar up by bending only your elbows.
Lower under control to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight.

exercises.name: Barbell glute bridge
cues: Lie on your back on the floor with a padded bar over your hips, knees bent, feet flat.
Tuck your pelvis slightly to engage the glutes.
Push your hips up with your glutes until your body forms a straight line from head to knees; squeeze at the top.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: Pad the bar with a mat, towel or barbell pad.

exercises.name: Barbell hack squat
cues: Stand in front of a barbell on the floor, bar behind your legs. Squat down and grip it with your arms outside your legs.
Breathe in, brace, back flat.
Stand up, keeping the bar close to the backs of your legs.
Lower with control and reset.
exercises.safety: Keep your back flat; the upright torso puts most of the work on the quads. Start light: the bar can scrape your calves and hamstrings.

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
cues: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a sturdy bench and roll the bar over your hips; pad the bar.
Feet flat about shoulder-width, knees bent; hold the bar steady.
Drive your hips up until your knees are at about 90° and your body is flat from shoulders to knees.
Lower under control.
exercises.safety: Use a pad, mat or towel between the bar and your pelvis. Don't over-arch your lower back at the top: finish with the glutes.

exercises.name: Barbell lunge
cues: Bar on your upper back as for a squat, feet hip-width, core braced.
Step forward, keeping your feet hip-width apart, and lower until your back knee nears the floor.
Push back to the start with your front leg.
exercises.safety: Balance is harder with a bar than with dumbbells, and you can't drop it: start light, and use the rack's safety arms or dumbbells instead. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Barbell preacher curl
cues: Set the pad so its top sits under your armpits with your arms resting on it; feet flat.
Grip the bar (or EZ bar) underhand and curl it up.
Lower under control as far as is comfortable.
Keep your upper arms on the pad and your body still.
exercises.safety: Keep the wrists straight. If full extension at the bottom feels uncomfortable, reverse a little earlier; never let the bar drop into the bottom.

exercises.name: Barbell rear-delt row
cues: Wide overhand grip. Hinge forward with a flat back and let the bar hang from straight arms.
Pull the bar high toward your upper chest with your upper arms pointing out to the sides.
Lower under control.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and no body swing. Your lower back holds the bent-over position, as in a barbell row.

exercises.name: Barbell roll-out (kneeling)
cues: Load a barbell with two plates of the same size so it rolls freely. Kneel on a soft pad, hands on the bar about shoulder-width, directly in front of your knees.
Brace and roll the bar forward as far as you can while keeping your back straight.
Reverse with control back to the start.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight; if your lower back sags, roll out less far. The reference allows a barbell that rolls freely in place of the ab wheel.

exercises.name: Barbell row
cues: Feet about shoulder-width, grip overhand slightly wider than your shoulders.
Push your hips back and lean forward, back flat (neither rounded nor arched), arms hanging straight.
Pull the bar to your lower chest or upper abs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower with control to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Your lower back holds the position the whole set. Swinging is most often a sign the weight is too heavy. Keep an eye on your total lower-back volume.

exercises.name: Barbell seated calf raise
cues: Sit on a bench, feet hip-width, with a barbell across your thighs just above your knees.
Put a plate or block under the balls of your feet for a longer range.
Press the weight up by lifting your heels.
Lower with control back to the start.
exercises.safety: Get a full stretch at the bottom and a full contraction at the top of each rep; no bouncing or short, choppy reps.

exercises.name: Barbell shrug
cues: Hold a barbell in front of your thighs with straight arms, overhand grip.
Raise your shoulders straight up as high as you can; pause briefly.
Lower them slowly.
exercises.safety: Straight up and down; don't roll the shoulders. Straps are fine if your grip gives out first.

exercises.name: Barbell standing calf raise
cues: Bar on your upper back; balls of your feet on a plate or step, heels hanging off.
Stand with your back near a wall so the plates touch it, which helps balance.
Lower your heels to a full stretch, then rise as high as you can with straight knees.
exercises.safety: Get a full stretch at the bottom and a full contraction at the top of each rep; no bouncing or short, choppy reps. Use the rack's safety arms or the Smith machine if balance is an issue.

exercises.name: Barbell step-up
cues: Bar on your upper back. Stand in front of a sturdy box or bench and put one whole foot on it.
Brace lightly and step up until that leg is straight.
Lower yourself with control, keeping that foot on the box.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Balance is harder with a bar than with dumbbells; start light and use a low box. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Barbell upright row
cues: Stand tall, grip the bar overhand with your hands closer than shoulder-width.
Pull the bar straight up toward your chin, close to your body, elbows out to the sides.
Stop before your upper arms go above shoulder height.
Lower the bar with control.
exercises.safety: Upright rows have a reputation for pinching the shoulder at the top: use light weights and few sets, keep your upper arms from going above shoulder height, and reverse earlier if your shoulders hurt. Lateral raises are an alternative.

exercises.name: Barbell walking lunge
cues: Bar on your upper back, core braced, with clear floor space in front of you.
Step forward into a lunge, back knee just above the floor.
Push up and bring the back foot forward straight into the next lunge.
Count reps per leg.
exercises.safety: Walking adds a balance challenge; master the stationary lunge first. Feet stay hip-width apart, not on one line.

exercises.name: Barbell wrist curl
cues: Sit with your forearms on your thighs, wrists just past your knees, barbell held palms up.
Let your hands drop and the bar roll out to your fingertips.
Close your grip and curl your wrists up.
exercises.safety: Keep the forearms still on your thighs; only the wrists move.

exercises.name: Barbell wrist curl behind the back
cues: Stand holding a barbell behind your back at arm's length, hands shoulder-width, palms facing back.
Open your hands and let the bar roll out into your fingers.
Close your grip and curl your wrists up. Only the hands and wrists move.
exercises.safety: Easiest to take the bar from a rack set at hip height and put it back there.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Barbell wrist curl behind the back

exercises.name: Barbell wrist curl over a bench
cues: Kneel facing a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists over the edge, barbell held underhand.
Lower your hands toward the floor and let the bar roll out into your fingers.
Close your grip and bend your wrists upward.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and a slow, full range.

exercises.name: Barbell wrist extension
cues: Sit with your forearms on your thighs, wrists just past your knees, barbell held palms down.
Lower your hands toward the floor.
Raise the backs of your hands as high as you can.
exercises.safety: Light weight, slow reps.

exercises.name: Barbell wrist extension over a bench
cues: Kneel facing a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists over the edge, barbell held overhand.
Lower your hands toward the floor.
Bend your wrists upward.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and slow, full reps.

exercises.name: Bent-over dumbbell row
cues: Stand with your feet about hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward at the hips with a neutral spine and brace your core; let the dumbbells hang from straight arms.
Pull them toward you as far as you can, elbows close to your sides, shoulder blades pulled back.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: No swinging with your upper body. The reference uses kettlebells; dumbbells hang from your hands the same way.

exercises.name: Bent-over reverse fly (head on bench)
cues: Stand behind an incline bench, feet about hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward with a straight back until your forehead rests on the top of the bench; let your arms hang toward the floor, palms facing in.
With just a slight bend at the elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are about level with your body.
Lower them back slowly.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight, no swinging or shrugging. The reference describes it standing bent over without a bench; resting your forehead only steadies your torso, the arms move the same way.

exercises.name: Bicycle crunch
cues: Lie on your back, hands behind your head, legs raised with knees bent to 90°.
Lift your head and shoulders, then extend one leg while rotating to bring the opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Alternate sides in a steady, controlled pedaling rhythm. Count reps per side.
exercises.safety: Rotate your torso; don't pull on your neck with your hands.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
cues: Feet about shoulder-width, hands behind your head or out in front.
Squat as deep as you can, chest up, knees tracking over your toes.
Stand back up.
exercises.safety: Mostly a warm-up or travel option: add a dumbbell (goblet squat) once 25 reps is easy.

exercises.name: Bodyweight triceps extension
cues: Set a bar in a rack, grip it overhand about shoulder-width and step back so you lean on it with straight arms, body straight like a standing plank.
Bend your elbows, bringing your torso forward and your head below the bar, slowly and under control.
Straighten your arms to return.
exercises.safety: A higher bar makes it easier; a lower bar harder.

exercises.name: Box squat
cues: Set a box or bench behind you at about parallel depth. Bar on your upper back as for a back squat.
Sit back and down until your glutes touch the box (or sit briefly with control).
Keep tension; don't relax or rock on the box.
Drive back up to standing.
exercises.safety: Control the descent; never drop onto the box. Set the safety arms as for a back squat.

exercises.name: Cable crossover (high to low)
cues: Set both pulleys high. Take the handles and step forward so the pulleys are slightly behind you; lean forward a little and brace.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Bring the handles down and together in front of your lower chest.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch, without letting the weights pull your arms back.
exercises.safety: Move slowly; if you need to swing your body to finish, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Cable curl
cues: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley, grip underhand about shoulder-width, and step back.
Curl the bar up by bending your elbows; upper arms still or slightly forward.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight.

exercises.name: Cable front raise
cues: Attach a handle to the low pulley and stand with your back to the machine, feet shoulder-width.
Hold the handle palm down, slight bend in the elbow, spine neutral.
Raise it straight forward to shoulder height without using your body.
Lower slowly. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: Cable glute kickback
cues: Attach an ankle strap to the low pulley and face the machine, holding it for support.
Brace your core and keep your body still.
Press the strapped leg back and up with your glute as far as you can without rotating your hips.
Return slowly. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: No swinging and no arching your lower back to get the leg higher. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Cable hip adduction
cues: Ankle strap on the low pulley. Stand side-on with the strapped leg nearest the machine; hold on for balance.
Core and glutes tight, slight bend in the standing leg.
Pull the strapped leg in and across in front of your standing leg, upper body still.
Return with control. Finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.safety: Start light; the inner thigh strains easily if you jerk the weight. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
cues: Attach a handle to the low pulley. Stand side-on, close to it, and hold the handle in the hand farther from the machine.
With control, raise your arm out to the side until your upper arm is horizontal.
Lower the handle with control. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: Cable pull-through
cues: Rope on the low pulley. Face away, straddle the cable, and walk forward a few steps; feet wide.
Hinge at the hips, knees slightly bent, letting the rope travel back between your thighs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, arms straight; the motion comes from the hips, not the arms.
Hinge back with control.
exercises.safety: Back flat throughout, as in any hinge.

exercises.name: Cable rear-delt row (rope)
cues: Rope on a high pulley. Grip overhand and step back one or two steps.
With your elbows high, pull the rope toward you so your upper arms move straight out to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Return with control.
exercises.safety: Start light: the point is feeling the rear delts work, not moving the most weight.

exercises.name: Cable rope hammer curl
cues: Attach a rope to the low pulley, grip it with palms facing each other, and step back.
Curl the rope up by bending your elbows; upper arms stay still.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight.

exercises.name: Cable upright row
cues: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley. Stand close, gripping it overhand with your hands closer than shoulder-width.
Pull the bar straight up toward your chin, close to your body, elbows out to the sides.
Stop before your upper arms go above shoulder height.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: The reference suggests the cable version if the barbell upright row is hard on your shoulders. Still: light weights, few sets, and reverse earlier if your shoulders hurt.

exercises.name: Cable wood chop (low to high)
cues: Set a handle at the lowest position, grip it with both hands, step away and stand side-on.
Arms almost straight throughout.
Sweep the handle diagonally up and across your body, rotating through your trunk.
Return under control. Finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.safety: Rotate through the trunk and hips smoothly; no jerking. One set = both sides.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Cable wood chop (low to high)

exercises.name: Captain's chair knee raise
cues: Rest your forearms on the arm pads, back against the back pad, legs hanging straight down.
Brace and raise your knees toward your chest; pause at the top.
Lower your legs under control.
exercises.safety: Slow and controlled; no swinging or momentum.

exercises.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
cues: Set an incline bench to 30–45° and lie chest-down, feet on the floor, dumbbells hanging.
Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, elbows close to your body.
Pause with your shoulder blades squeezed together; don't shrug.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.safety: The bench takes some stress off your lower back. The reference rows both dumbbells at once; the photos show one arm.

exercises.name: Chin-up
cues: Hang from the bar with palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart.
Chest up, eyes on the bar, shoulders drawn down.
Pull until your chin clears the bar or the bar touches your upper chest.
Lower with control to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Most people are a little stronger at chin-ups than pull-ups. Use a band under your feet or knees to make it easier.

exercises.name: Close-grip bench press
cues: Lie on the bench, pull your shoulder blades together and down, feet planted.
Grip narrower than a regular bench press, hands about directly above your shoulders.
Lower with control until the bar touches your chest around where the ribs end.
Press back up to the start.
exercises.safety: Set the safety arms or use a spotter. Expect to use less weight than your regular bench.

exercises.name: Close-grip lat pulldown
cues: Grip the bar overhand, hands narrower than your shoulders. Sit with your thighs under the pad.
Chest up, lean back slightly, eyes on the bar.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are fully straight.
exercises.safety: Pull to the front only, never behind your neck. Don't rock your torso to move the weight.

exercises.name: Close-grip push-up
cues: Push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Body in a straight line, abs lightly braced.
Lower as far as you can with your elbows close to your sides.
Push back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Too hard? Put your hands on a bench.

exercises.name: Concentration curl
cues: Sit on a bench, lean forward, and brace the back of your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder; only the elbow moves.
Lower under control. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Hard to cheat on, so keep the weight modest. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: Crunch
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent to about 90°, hands in front of your chest (the photos show them behind the head).
Lift your upper body by contracting your abs and bending forward.
Bend as far forward as you can while your lower back stays on the floor, then return to the start.
exercises.safety: Hold a weight against your chest to make it harder.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: Lie on your back, arms straight up, knees bent 90° over your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor and brace.
Slowly straighten one leg toward the floor while lowering the opposite arm overhead.
Return and switch sides. Count reps per side.
exercises.safety: Your lower back must stay on the floor the whole time; reduce the reach if it lifts.

exercises.name: Deadlift
cues: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, hands about shoulder-width, arms straight like ropes.
Breathe in, brace, chest up, and take the slack out of the bar before it leaves the floor.
Push the floor away, extending your knees and hips, and pull the bar close up your legs until you stand tall with hips and knees locked out.
Lower by pushing your hips back first, then bend your knees once the bar passes them. Reset your breath each rep.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. Wear flat, firm shoes. Don't let your hips shoot up before the bar moves.

exercises.name: Decline barbell bench press
cues: Hook your legs under the pads, lie back, pull your shoulder blades together and down, chest up.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and unrack to straight arms.
Lower with control until the bar touches your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Set the safety arms or use a spotter: on a decline you can't roll a stuck bar off. Your head is below your hips, so skip it if that makes you light-headed.

exercises.name: Decline chest press machine
cues: Adjust the seat to fit you, sit down and grip the handles.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.
Bring them back to the start with control.
exercises.safety: The reference covers machine chest presses in general; follow the machine's placard for setup.

exercises.name: Decline dumbbell press
cues: Set the bench to a decline and lock your legs under the pads. Lie back and lift the dumbbells to straight arms.
Press to straight arms over your lower chest.
Lower with control back to your shoulders.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench.
exercises.safety: Getting in and out is the hard part on a decline: start light, and finish with the dumbbells on your chest before sitting up.

exercises.name: Decline push-up
cues: Feet on a box or bench, hands slightly wider than your shoulders on the floor.
Body in one straight line from head to heels; brace your abs.
Lower yourself as deep as you can.
Push back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Raising the feet puts more of your bodyweight on your arms; master the floor push-up first.

exercises.name: Decline Smith machine press
cues: Put a decline bench under the Smith bar so the bar comes down over your lower chest; hook your legs under the pads.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, pull your shoulder blades together and down, and unhook the bar.
Lower with control until the bar touches your chest.
Press back up.
exercises.safety: Set the stoppers just below where the bar touches your chest. Your head is below your hips; skip it if that makes you light-headed. The reference covers the free-barbell decline press; the rails only guide the bar.

exercises.name: Deficit deadlift
cues: Stand on a low platform or a weight plate, the bar over the middle of your feet.
Breathe in, lean forward and grip the bar.
Hold your breath, brace, and pull the bar close to your body with a straight back until you stand straight.
Lower the bar to the floor with control; breathe and repeat.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. The deficit makes the lift harder and works the quads more: use less weight than your normal deadlift.

exercises.name: Drag curl
cues: Hold a barbell underhand at shoulder-width, feet shoulder-width.
Drive your elbows back so the bar drags up along your body.
Stop at upper-chest height with your forearms about level with the floor.
Lower slowly along the same path.
exercises.safety: Shoulders stay down and torso still; the bar never swings out in front.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
cues: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to your chest. Feet flat, shoulder blades back and down.
Press up to straight arms over your chest, palms facing your feet.
Lower with control back to your shoulders.
Keep your upper back and hips on the bench throughout.
exercises.safety: Start lighter than you would with a barbell: dumbbells need more balance. When you finish, bring them to your chest before sitting up.

exercises.name: Dumbbell curl
cues: Stand tall with the dumbbells at your sides, palms facing forward, elbows close to your body.
Curl both dumbbells up by bending only your elbows.
Lower under control to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
cues: Sit on the floor, legs straight, dumbbells in your hip creases. Lie down while you bring them up to your chest.
Press to straight arms, then bend your knees and put your feet flat on the floor.
Lower slowly until your upper arms touch the floor, then press back up.
Finish the set by gently setting the dumbbells down on the floor.
exercises.safety: Your upper arms stop against the floor, so the range is shorter than a bench press.

exercises.name: Dumbbell fly
cues: Lie on a flat bench, feet flat, shoulder blades tucked, chest up. Hold the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in your elbows, held the same the whole time, lower the weights out to your sides.
Go as deep as you can with control.
Bring them back up to the start. Don't let the elbows bend more: that turns the fly into a press.
exercises.safety: Start light: the load gets heavy fast in the bottom position, and too much weight there risks injury.

exercises.name: Dumbbell front raise
cues: Stand tall holding the dumbbells on straight arms in front of your hips.
With control, raise them forward with straight arms to shoulder height (the second photo goes higher than needed).
Lower under control. No swinging from the hips.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lunge
cues: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, feet hip-width, core braced.
Step forward far enough that both knees can bend to about 90°; keep your feet hip-width apart, not in line.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor.
Push back to the start with your front leg. Alternate legs or finish one side first.
exercises.safety: Front knee tracks over your toes, foot flat. Too short a step overloads the front knee. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Dumbbell preacher curl (two arms)
cues: Use a preacher bench (or a bench backrest tilted back slightly) and rest your upper arms on the pad, a dumbbell in each hand.
Lower the dumbbells as far as you can with control.
Curl them back up to the start.
exercises.safety: If full extension feels uncomfortable at the bottom, reverse a little earlier.

exercises.name: Dumbbell pullover
cues: Lie with your upper back across a bench, feet flat, hips level with the bench. Hold one dumbbell over your chest with both hands.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbell back behind your head in an arc until your arms are in line with your body, or to a comfortable stretch.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc.
exercises.safety: Go light and control the bottom: the stretch loads the shoulder. Hold the dumbbell securely by the inside of the top plate.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, arms straight and relaxed, core tight.
Lift your shoulders straight up as high as you can and pause briefly.
Lower slowly.
exercises.safety: Move from the shoulders only, straight up and down. Straps let your traps, not your grip, set the weight.

exercises.name: Dumbbell side bend
cues: Stand with feet shoulder-width, a dumbbell in one hand, the other hand on your hip.
Bend slowly straight to the dumbbell side, sliding it down your leg to a comfortable depth.
Come back up using the obliques on the other side. Finish the reps, then switch.
exercises.safety: Stay in one plane: don't lean forward or back. No momentum. One set = both sides.

exercises.name: Dumbbell squat
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet about shoulder-width.
Breathe in, brace lightly, and squat down as deep as you can with your chest up and back flat.
Stand back up, breathing out.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique. Easy to bail: just drop the dumbbells.

exercises.name: Dumbbell standing calf raise
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand (or one, holding a rail with the other); balls of your feet on a step.
Lower your heels to a full stretch with straight knees.
Rise as high as you can.
exercises.safety: Get a full stretch at the bottom and a full contraction at the top of each rep; no bouncing or short, choppy reps. For an added challenge, do one leg at a time holding one dumbbell, the other hand on a wall or rail.

exercises.name: Dumbbell step-up
cues: Stand facing a sturdy bench or box with a dumbbell in each hand; put one whole foot on it.
Brace lightly and step up until the working leg is straight, pushing through the top foot (not the back one).
Lower under control, keeping the working foot on the box.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Use a box low enough that your knee isn't above your hip when you start. Make sure it can't slide. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Dumbbell upright row
cues: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Pull them up close to your body, elbows leading out to the sides.
Stop before your upper arms go above shoulder height.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: The reference covers the barbell version; the same rules apply: light weights, few sets, upper arms no higher than your shoulders, and reverse earlier if your shoulders hurt.

exercises.name: Dumbbell wrist curl
cues: Kneel or sit with your forearms on a bench, hands past the edge, dumbbells held palms up.
Lower your hands and let the dumbbells roll out to your fingers.
Close your grip and curl your wrists up as far as you can.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and a slow, full range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell wrist extension
cues: Rest your forearms on a bench, hands past the edge, dumbbells held palms down.
Lower your hands toward the floor.
Raise the backs of your hands as high as you can.
exercises.safety: Use much less weight than for wrist curls; slow, full reps.

exercises.name: EZ-bar curl
cues: Grip the EZ bar underhand on the angled parts, feet about hip-width, core braced.
Curl the bar toward your chest with your elbows close to your body; pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to the start.
exercises.safety: Don't let your elbows drift forward. If you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight. The angled grip can be kinder to the wrists and elbows.

exercises.name: EZ-bar lying triceps extension
cues: Lie on a bench with your head near the end. Hold the EZ bar over your chest with straight arms, shoulder-width grip.
Bend only your elbows and lower the bar behind your head (not to your forehead).
Keep the elbows the same width apart throughout.
Extend back to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Keep your elbows the same width apart throughout; letting them flare out is stressful for the shoulder. Heavy, low-rep sets are often uncomfortable here, so stay around 8–15 reps. Lowering behind the head (rather than to the forehead) gives a longer range of motion.

exercises.name: Face pull
cues: Rope on a high pulley (about forehead height). Grip overhand and step back one or two steps; stand tall, glutes and core tight.
With your elbows held high, pull the rope toward your forehead, your upper arms moving straight out to your sides.
Rotate your forearms up as you pull.
Let your arms go forward slowly.
exercises.safety: Too much weight turns it into a row toward the chest; keep it light enough to keep the elbows high.

exercises.name: Front squat
cues: Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and rest the bar on the front of your shoulders, on top of your collarbones.
Breathe in, brace, unrack and take two steps back.
Squat as deep as you can with your torso upright and elbows up.
Stand back up, breathing out on the way.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique. Needs wrist, shoulder and ankle mobility; crossing your arms with your hands on top of the bar, or using straps, helps if the wrists complain. Set the safety arms.

exercises.name: Glute-ham raise
cues: Set the machine so your knees rest on the support pad and your feet are locked under the footplate.
Body straight from knees to head, core braced, arms across your chest.
Bend at the knees and lower yourself slowly until your body is nearly parallel to the floor.
Pull yourself back up with your hamstrings and glutes.
exercises.safety: Very demanding: push off lightly with your hands at the bottom if you can't pull all the way up yet. Keep it controlled.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold a dumbbell (or kettlebell) vertically against your chest, feet about shoulder-width.
Breathe in, brace lightly, and squat as deep as you can with your chest up.
Stand back up, breathing out.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique. Your arms usually tire before your legs; when they do, move on to a front or back squat.

exercises.name: Good morning
cues: Bar on your upper back as for a squat. Unrack and step back, feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Breathe in, brace, and push your hips back as far as you can, knees slightly bent.
Lean forward as far as you can with a flat back, without the bar rolling forward.
Reverse by driving your hips forward to stand.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. Start very light; the lever arm makes small weights feel heavy. Set the safety arms in case you have to drop the bar.

exercises.name: Hack squat machine
cues: Set the shoulder pads, back flat against the pad. Feet about shoulder-width, slightly in front of the sled's base.
Release the safety handles.
Squat as deep as you can with good form, then push back up.
Re-engage the safety handles when you finish.
exercises.safety: Lower feet on the platform shift work to the quads; higher feet to the glutes. If the machine doesn't fit you comfortably, use another squat.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
cues: Stand with the dumbbells at your sides, palms facing each other.
Curl them up keeping the palms facing each other (thumbs up), upper arms close to your body.
Lower under control.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight. Don't twist the wrists.

exercises.name: Handstand push-up (wall)
cues: Hands shoulder-width on the floor, fingers forward, close to a wall.
Kick up into a handstand against the wall; your heels can rest lightly on it.
Brace your core and lower your head toward the floor with control.
Press back up by straightening your elbows.
exercises.safety: An advanced exercise that's tricky to master. Only do it if you can hold a wall handstand comfortably.

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise
cues: Hang from a bar high enough that your legs hang straight.
Raise your legs (or knees, to make it easier) as high as you can in front of you, curling your pelvis up at the top.
Lower under control without swinging.
exercises.safety: Slow and controlled; no swinging or momentum. The hip flexors work hard here too; bending the knees makes it easier.

exercises.name: High row machine
cues: Adjust the seat so you fit the machine and can reach the handles with straight arms.
Pull the handles toward you as far as possible, along the machine's path.
Slowly return the handles to the start.
exercises.safety: The reference covers machine rows in general, not this machine's exact path; follow the machine's placard for setup.

exercises.name: Hip abduction machine
cues: Sit against the backrest with your outer thighs against the pads, feet flat, knees at about 90°.
Press outward as far as you can without straining; squeeze your glutes at the end.
Return slowly; control the weight rather than letting it pull you back.
exercises.safety: Mainly trains the gluteus medius and minimus (the outer hip).

exercises.name: Incline barbell bench press
cues: Set the bench to about 30–45°. Feet flat, shoulder blades back and down, chest up.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders and unrack to straight arms over your shoulders.
Lower with control to the upper chest, just below the collarbones.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Set the safety arms just below chest height or use a spotter, and keep your thumbs wrapped around the bar. A much steeper bench turns it into a shoulder press.

exercises.name: Incline barbell triceps extension
cues: Set an incline bench to 30–45°, lie back, feet flat, narrow overhand grip.
Start with the bar over your shoulders, elbows close together.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar until it's slightly behind your head.
Extend fully back to the start.
exercises.safety: Keep your elbows the same width apart throughout; letting them flare out is stressful for the shoulder. Heavy, low-rep sets are often uncomfortable here, so stay around 8–15 reps. Don't arch your lower back.

exercises.name: Incline chest press machine
cues: Adjust the seat to fit you, sit down with your back against the pad, and grip the handles.
Press the handles until your arms are straight.
Bring them back to the start with control.
exercises.safety: Don't let the plates or stack slam between reps.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
cues: Set a bench to 45–60° and sit back with the dumbbells hanging straight down at your sides, palms forward.
Keep your shoulders down and back against the bench; don't bring them forward as you curl.
Keep your upper arms still and curl the dumbbells up, moving only your forearms.
Lower back to the start.
exercises.safety: Expect incline curls to feel much heavier than standing curls; start lighter.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell fly
cues: Set the bench to a slight incline. Hold the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in your elbows, held the same the whole time, lower the weights out to your sides.
Go as deep as you can with control.
Bring them back up to the start.
exercises.safety: Start light: the load gets heavy fast in the bottom position, and too much weight there risks injury.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
cues: Hands slightly wider than your shoulders on a bench or box.
Head, hips and heels in one straight line; brace your abs lightly.
Lower until your chest touches the edge, elbows about 45° from your body.
Push back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: The higher the surface, the easier it is: use it to build up to floor push-ups.

exercises.name: Incline-bench reverse fly
cues: Lie face down on a bench inclined to about 30–45°, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing in.
Let your arms hang with a slight elbow bend.
Raise the weights out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Reverse dumbbell flyes on incline bench

exercises.name: Inverted row
cues: Set a bar in a rack high enough that you can hang below it on straight arms with your heels on the floor. Overhand grip, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest up to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower with control to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Raise the bar to make it easier; put your feet on a bench to make it harder. Check the bar is seated securely in the rack.

exercises.name: Jackknife sit-up (V-up)
cues: Lie on your back, arms straight overhead, legs straight.
Lift your legs and upper body together, reaching your hands toward your toes into a "V".
Pause briefly and lower with control, without letting your feet or arms touch the floor between reps.
exercises.safety: Demanding on balance and the hip flexors; bend the knees slightly if needed.

exercises.name: Kettlebell front squat
cues: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders, feet shoulder-width.
Brace, chest up, shoulders back.
Sit down between your heels as deep as your mobility allows, kettlebells steady.
Stand back up.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique.

exercises.name: Kettlebell press (two arms)
cues: Stand with feet a bit wider than your shoulders, kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders.
Breathe in and brace lightly, chest up.
Press until your arms are straight and your upper arms are beside your ears.
Lower slowly back to the rack position.
exercises.safety: Shoulders neither shrugged nor jammed down; press in whatever path between forward and sideways feels comfortable.

exercises.name: Kneeling glute kickback
cues: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
Keeping one knee bent at 90°, press that foot toward the ceiling, squeezing the glute.
Lower without touching the floor. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Keep your back flat; don't arch to lift higher. Use the cable version for more resistance.

exercises.name: Kneeling one-arm pulldown
cues: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and kneel facing it, arm straight up holding the handle.
Chest up, eyes slightly up.
Pull the handle down toward your side.
Return slowly until your arm is straight again. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: The reference does this seated with thighs under a pad; kneeling, the arm moves the same way. Don't twist to finish. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: Landmine rotation
cues: Set a barbell in a landmine (or wedge the end securely in a corner). Stand facing it, feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Hold the end of the bar with both hands, arms straight in front of you at about shoulder height.
Brace your core and, keeping your arms straight, turn your hips and torso together to sweep the bar down toward the outside of one hip.
Rotate back across and down to the other side. Alternate sides with control and do the same number each way.
exercises.safety: Start light. Turn your hips and torso together and keep the movement controlled; no jerking at the turn.

exercises.name: Leg extension
cues: Line up your knee with the machine's pivot and set the back pad so your back rests against it; ankle pad just above your feet.
Brace your core and extend your legs with control until straight.
Lower slowly, using the longest range you can.
exercises.safety: Don't snap or hyperextend your knees at the top, and don't let your lower back arch off the pad.

exercises.name: Leg press calf raise
cues: Sit in the leg press with the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, heels hanging off.
Unrack with knees very slightly bent, and keep them there.
Lower your heels under control as far as your ankles comfortably allow, then press through the balls of your feet, heels as high as possible.
exercises.safety: Get a full stretch at the bottom and a full contraction at the top of each rep; no bouncing or short, choppy reps. On a 45° leg press, make sure the safety bars are in place: they save you if a foot slips off the platform.

exercises.name: Low cable crossover (low to high)
cues: Set both pulleys low. Take the handles and step forward so the cables run from behind you; stand tall and brace.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Sweep the handles up and together in front of your upper chest, about chin height.
Lower slowly back to the stretch.
exercises.safety: Keep it a fly: if your elbows bend more as you lift, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Lying cable curl (bench, high pulley)
cues: Put a bench in front of a high pulley with a straight bar. Lie on it with your head at the end nearest the machine.
Grip the bar underhand, arms straight toward the pulley.
Keep your upper arms still and curl the bar toward your head; pause briefly.
Return slowly to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay still; only the elbows bend.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Lying bicep cable curl on bench

exercises.name: Lying cable curl (floor)
cues: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and lie on the floor, head away from the machine.
Grip the bar underhand, arms straight along the floor.
Keep your upper arms still and curl the bar toward your shoulders; pause briefly.
Return slowly to the start.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay still on the floor; only the elbows bend.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Lying bicep cable curl on floor

exercises.name: Lying dumbbell triceps extension
cues: Lie on a bench, head near the end, dumbbells held straight up over your shoulders.
Bend only your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head.
Keep the elbows the same distance apart throughout.
Extend back to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Keep your elbows the same width apart throughout; letting them flare out is stressful for the shoulder. Heavy, low-rep sets are often uncomfortable here, so stay around 8–15 reps.

exercises.name: Lying leg curl
cues: Lie face down and line your knees up with the machine's pivot; pad just above your heels.
Curl the pad up as far as you can.
Lower it slowly to straight legs.
exercises.safety: Keep your hips down on the bench; lifting them to finish means the weight is too heavy.

refs.title: StrengthLog: How to train your hamstrings

exercises.name: Lying leg raise
cues: Lie on your back on a bench (or the floor), hands holding the bench behind your head or at your sides.
Keeping your legs straight, lift them until they point straight up.
Lower them slowly, stopping before your lower back arches off the bench.
exercises.safety: Bend your knees slightly to make it easier. If your lower back lifts off, shorten the lowering.

exercises.name: Lying neck curl (plate)
cues: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your head slightly past the end.
Put a folded towel on your forehead and hold a plate on it with both hands; the hands only balance it, they don't lift.
Tuck your chin slightly and keep it tucked, then curl your head toward your chest without lifting your shoulders.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly back to the start.
exercises.safety: Your neck is sensitive: start very light, move slowly and avoid extreme ranges. Do neck work at the end of a workout. If you've had neck or cervical spine problems, see a doctor or physio first.

exercises.name: Lying neck extension (plate)
cues: Lie face down on a flat bench, chest and stomach supported, head just off the end; feet on the floor for balance.
Hold a plate on the back of your head with both hands (a folded towel underneath is more comfortable).
Start with your chin slightly tucked and your neck neutral, then raise the back of your head toward the ceiling.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly back to the start. No jerky movements.
exercises.safety: Your neck is sensitive: start very light, move slowly and avoid extreme ranges (the first photo drops the head further than needed). Do neck work at the end of a workout. If you've had neck or cervical spine problems, see a doctor or physio first.

exercises.name: Machine chest fly
cues: Adjust the back support and handles so you grip them at shoulder height with a full range of motion; the machine's pivot should line up with your shoulders.
Chest up, core braced, back against the backrest the whole time.
With a slight, fixed bend in your arms, push the handles forward until they meet in front of your body.
Let them go back to the start slowly and under control.
exercises.safety: A seat set too high or too low strains the shoulders. No momentum to start a rep.

exercises.name: Machine overhead triceps extension
cues: Set the seat so the handles line up with or a little above your shoulders; arms on the pads.
Hold the handles with your elbows close to your head.
Extend your elbows until your arms are fully straight.
Bend them back down with control.
exercises.safety: Only the elbows move.

exercises.name: Machine row (chest-supported)
cues: Set the seat so the handles are at about chest height, and rest your chest on the pad.
Grip the handles with straight arms, shoulders relaxed.
Pull the handles toward you as far as possible, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.safety: Keep your chest on the pad; leaning back to finish means the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip dumbbell bench press
cues: Lie on a flat bench, feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back, dumbbells held with palms facing each other.
Start with straight arms above you.
Lower the dumbbells with control back to your shoulders.
Press them back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: The reference doesn't prescribe a grip; this is the same press with palms facing each other.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip incline dumbbell press
cues: Set the bench to 30–45°. Sit and lift the dumbbells to the start, palms facing each other.
Shoulder blades back, whole feet on the floor.
Start with the dumbbells straight above your shoulders and lower them with control.
Press back up to fully straight arms; keep your wrists straight.
exercises.safety: Too upright a bench turns it into a shoulder press. The reference doesn't prescribe a grip; this is the same press with palms facing each other.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip pulldown (V-bar)
cues: Attach a V-handle (close neutral grip). Sit with thighs under the pad.
Chest up, eyes up at the handle.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, elbows close to your sides.
Return slowly to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Keep your torso still; if you have to swing back, lighten it.

exercises.name: Nordic hamstring curl (lowering)
cues: Kneel with your hips straight and your feet wedged under something that can't move.
Lean forward by straightening your knees, without pushing your hips back.
Fight the fall with your hamstrings for as long as you can (aim for about 2 seconds).
When your chest reaches the floor, push yourself back up with your arms.
exercises.safety: Only the lowering is the exercise; catch yourself with your hands at the bottom.

exercises.name: Oblique crunch
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, hands at the sides of your head (the photos rest the calves on a bench instead).
Lift your shoulders and twist so one elbow moves diagonally toward the opposite knee; pause.
Lower without fully relaxing, then repeat or alternate sides.
exercises.safety: Don't pull on your neck with your hands. When you can do more reps than planned, hold a plate or dumbbell to your chest.

exercises.name: One-arm cable crossover
cues: Set both pulleys high and take a handle in each hand. Step forward, lean slightly forward and brace, hands together in front of you.
Keep one arm in place and let the other open out to the side with a slight, fixed elbow bend.
Bring it back in until the hands meet. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Move slowly and don't swing your body. The reference describes both arms together; one at a time, each arm moves the same way. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm cable curl
cues: Attach a single handle to the low pulley. Hold it underhand in one hand and step back so the weight lifts off the stack.
Upper arm still at your side; put your other hand on your waist for balance.
Curl the handle up by bending your elbow, then lower with control. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Upper arms stay at your sides (or drift slightly forward); if you have to swing, the weight is too heavy. Keep your wrists straight. The reference uses a bar with both hands; one arm at a time with a handle, the elbow moves the same way. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell bench press
cues: Lie on a flat bench and bring one dumbbell up to straight arm over your chest.
Lower it with control back to your shoulder.
Press it back up to a straight arm. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: The reference presses two dumbbells; one at a time, each arm moves the same way, but your body has to resist twisting: start light. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell fly
cues: Lie on a flat bench, feet flat, one dumbbell held above your chest.
With a slight bend in your elbow, held the same the whole time, lower it out to the side as deep as you can with control.
Bring it back to the start. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Start light: the load gets heavy fast in the bottom position. The reference uses two dumbbells; one at a time, each arm moves the same way. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Stand tall holding a dumbbell at your side; hold something steady with the other hand.
With a slight elbow bend, lift the dumbbell out to the side until your upper arm is horizontal; no higher.
Lower it with control. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging. The reference raises both arms; one at a time, each arm moves the same way. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell preacher curl
cues: Rest the back of your upper arm on the preacher pad, dumbbell in hand, palm up.
Curl the dumbbell up; the upper arm stays on the pad.
Lower slowly to a comfortable full stretch. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and control the bottom; don't let the elbow snap straight. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
cues: One hand and the same-side knee on a bench, back flat and level with the floor, other foot on the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang from a straight arm; eyes on the floor to keep your neck neutral.
Drive your elbow up toward the ceiling, pulling the dumbbell toward your hip. Elbow close to your body.
Lower with control to a full stretch. Finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.safety: No jerking or twisting. Straps are fine if your grip gives out first.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Stand with one dumbbell at your shoulder.
Breathe in and lightly brace your core.
Press it up to a straight arm.
Lower it with control back to your shoulder. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Pressing one arm at a time works the obliques more. No leaning to the side. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm kettlebell floor press
cues: Lie on the floor with a kettlebell at your chest, upper arm on the floor.
Press it to a straight arm, then bend your knees and put your feet flat.
Lower it slowly until your upper arm touches the floor, then press again.
Finish the reps, then switch arms; set the kettlebell down gently at the end.
exercises.safety: The reference uses a kettlebell in each hand; one at a time, each arm moves the same way. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm kettlebell row
cues: Stand with a kettlebell in front of your feet, feet about hip-width.
Hinge forward at the hips with a neutral spine and brace your core; grab the kettlebell.
Pull it toward you as far as you can, elbow close to your side, shoulder blade pulled back.
Lower with control. Finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.safety: No swinging with your upper body. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm lat pulldown
cues: Attach a single handle. Sit (or kneel) under the pulley holding it in one hand, arm straight overhead.
Chest up, eyes slightly up.
Pull the handle down to the side of your chest, elbow down toward your hip.
Return slowly to a full stretch. Finish all reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: One set = both arms. Don't twist your torso to finish a rep.

exercises.name: One-arm overhead cable triceps extension
cues: Attach a single handle to the low pulley. Face away from the machine and use both hands to lift the handle into place behind your head, then hold it in one hand, palm forward.
Upper arm vertical next to your head; your other hand can steady the elbow.
Straighten your arm fully, moving only the forearm.
Lower back behind your head into the stretch. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Keep your elbows the same width apart throughout; letting them flare out is stressful for the shoulder. Heavy, low-rep sets are often uncomfortable here, so stay around 8–15 reps. The reference uses a rope with both hands; one arm at a time with a handle, the elbow moves the same way. One set = both arms.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Overhead cable triceps extension (lower position)

exercises.name: One-arm overhead dumbbell extension
cues: Stand and press one dumbbell to a straight arm over your head.
Keeping your upper arm still and vertical, lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Extend your arm again. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm preacher curl over a bench
cues: Tilt a bench backrest back slightly. Stand behind it with a dumbbell and rest your upper arm on the backrest.
Lower the dumbbell as far as you can with control.
Curl it back up. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: If full extension feels uncomfortable, reverse a little earlier. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-arm seated cable row
cues: Sit at the low-row station with a single handle, feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
Start with your arm straight and your torso leaning slightly forward; let the shoulder blade slide forward.
Pull the handle toward the side of your stomach, elbow close to your body, leaning back slightly and pulling the shoulder blade back.
Return slowly to the stretch. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Only a slight lean forward and back: don't heave with your lower back. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: One-leg leg extension
cues: Set the machine so your knee lines up with the pivot.
Extend one leg with control until it's straight; the other leg relaxes.
Lower slowly. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Use the longest comfortable range; no snapping at the top. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Overhead barbell triceps extension
cues: Grip a light barbell (or EZ bar) narrow and lift it to straight arms overhead; feet shoulder-width, core braced.
Upper arms still and vertical.
Lower the bar behind your head as far as your mobility allows.
Extend back overhead.
exercises.safety: Keep your elbows the same width apart throughout; letting them flare out is stressful for the shoulder. Heavy, low-rep sets are often uncomfortable here, so stay around 8–15 reps. Keep a neutral spine; don't arch your lower back.

exercises.name: Overhead dumbbell triceps extension
cues: Hold one dumbbell with both hands (by the top plate) and press it to straight arms overhead.
Keep your upper arms still and vertical, close to your head.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head as far as is comfortable.
Extend back to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Keep your elbows the same width apart throughout; letting them flare out is stressful for the shoulder. Heavy, low-rep sets are often uncomfortable here, so stay around 8–15 reps. Brace your core so your lower back doesn't arch.

exercises.name: Overhead press (barbell)
cues: Set the bar in a rack at about chest height. Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, unrack it onto your front delts and step back.
Feet about hip-width, glutes and core lightly braced.
Press straight up, moving your head back slightly to let the bar pass, then bring your head through once it's overhead.
Lower under control to your front shoulders. Legs stay still (using them makes it a push press).
exercises.safety: Doing too much too soon is the main overuse risk: start light and add weight and sets gradually.

exercises.name: Pallof press
cues: Set a handle on the cable at chest height and stand side-on, feet hip-width, knees slightly bent.
Hold the handle at your chest with both hands and brace.
Press it straight out in front of you without letting your torso turn; hold briefly.
Bring it back to your chest. Finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.safety: The point is not moving: pick a weight you can resist without twisting. One set = both sides.

exercises.name: Pin bench press
cues: Set the rack's safety pins so the bar stops just above your chest.
Lie on the bench, shoulder blades together and down, grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Breathe in, brace and unrack. Lower with control until the bar touches the pins.
Press back up, keeping your body tight even at the bottom.
exercises.safety: Mostly a strength tool for the top of the bench press.

exercises.name: Pistol squat
cues: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended straight out in front of you.
Chest up, core braced, arms (or a light kettlebell) held forward for balance.
Bend the standing leg and squat as low as you can while staying balanced and in control; keep the other leg straight and off the floor.
Press through your standing heel to stand up. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Very demanding on balance and strength. The reference describes it with arms forward; the photos hold a kettlebell in front. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Plank
cues: Rest on your forearms and toes, elbows directly under your shoulders.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes; body in a straight line from head to heels.
Hold for the target time. Log the seconds held in the reps box.
exercises.safety: Stop when your hips sag or pike. Moving your elbows a little further forward makes it harder.

exercises.name: Plate front raise
cues: Hold a plate by its edges at about 3 and 9 o'clock, arms straight in front of your hips.
Raise it forward with straight arms to shoulder height.
Lower slowly under control.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging.

exercises.name: Plate pinch
cues: Put two plates together, smooth sides facing out.
Pinch them with your fingers on one side and your thumb on the other, and lift them off the floor.
Hold as long as you can, then put them down under control. Log the seconds held; switch hands.
exercises.safety: The plates' surface and chalk change how much you can hold a lot; compare like with like.

exercises.name: Pull-up
cues: Hang from the bar, palms facing away, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Chest up, eyes on the bar. Start the pull by drawing your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull until your chin clears the bar or the bar touches your upper chest.
Lower with control all the way to straight arms; let your shoulder blades rise at the bottom.
exercises.safety: Strict reps only, no kipping. Can't do 5? Use the assisted pull-up machine or a band. Log added weight (belt) in the weight box.

exercises.name: Push-up
cues: Hands slightly wider than your shoulders, body in one straight line from head to heels, abs lightly braced.
Lower yourself as deep as you can, until your chest touches the floor.
Push back up to straight arms without letting your hips sag or pike.
exercises.safety: Too hard for the target reps? Put your hands on a bench (incline push-up). Too easy? Feet on a box, or a plate on your back.

exercises.name: Rack pull
cues: Set the bar on the rack pins (or blocks) between just below and just above knee height, over the middle of your feet.
Lean forward with a slight knee bend and grip just outside your legs.
Brace, then pull the bar close to your body with a flat back until you stand tall.
Lower under control back to the pins.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. You can lift more than from the floor, so add weight gradually.

exercises.name: Reverse barbell curl
cues: Grip the bar overhand (palms down) about shoulder-width.
Curl it up by bending your elbows; upper arms at your sides.
Lower under control, keeping tension at the bottom.
exercises.safety: You'll use much less weight than a normal curl. Keep the wrists straight.

exercises.name: Reverse cable fly
cues: Set both pulleys high. Cross over to take the opposite handles and stand centered between them.
Arms forward with a slight elbow bend, chest up, core braced, shoulders back and down.
Pull your arms back out to the sides until they're roughly in line with your body.
Return slowly under control.
exercises.safety: Light weight and slow reps. Swinging or arching your lower back strains the back and shoulders.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
cues: Lie on your back, arms out to your sides, palms down.
Brace and lift your feet so your knees are directly above your hips, bent to 90°.
Slowly curl your hips off the mat, rolling your pelvis toward your ribs without changing the knee angle; pause when your spine can't roll further.
Roll back down slowly until your hips touch the mat with your knees back over your hips.
exercises.safety: Control the way down to protect your lower back, and don't let your knees drift past your hips or swing your legs for momentum.

exercises.name: Reverse dumbbell curl
cues: Hold the dumbbells at your sides with palms facing back/down.
Curl them up keeping that grip, elbows at your sides.
Lower under control.
exercises.safety: Don't let the elbows drift back to cheat the weight up.

exercises.name: Reverse dumbbell lunge
cues: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, feet about shoulder-width.
Step far back and lower into a lunge as deep as you can.
Don't let your back knee hit the floor.
Push back up to standing with the front leg.
exercises.safety: One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Reverse hyperextension
cues: Lie face down on the machine (or a high bench) with your hips at the edge, legs hanging, hands holding the handles.
Legs straight and together, core braced, back neutral.
Raise your legs until they're in line with your body or slightly above; squeeze your glutes and hold a moment.
Lower slowly under control. No swinging.
exercises.safety: Slow and controlled; don't swing your legs up or down.

exercises.name: Ring dip
cues: Grip the rings about shoulder-width apart and jump up to straight arms.
Lower yourself with control until your shoulders are below your elbows, or as deep as you comfortably can.
Push back up to the start.
exercises.safety: Dips can be stressful on the shoulders and sternum if you're not used to them: build volume very gradually. A partner lifting your legs or a dip machine makes it easier; a belt with weight, harder.

exercises.name: Ring or strap row
cues: Set the rings (or suspension straps) to the height you want and grip them, facing the anchor.
Lean back on straight arms and walk your feet forward until your body is at an angle, straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest toward the rings by driving your elbows back, core tight.
Lower yourself slowly back to the start.
exercises.safety: The more upright you stand, the easier it is.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift (barbell)
cues: Start standing with the bar (lift it from the floor or a rack), hands just outside your legs.
Brace, then hinge at the hips with your knees almost straight (a slight bend), sliding the bar down the front of your thighs.
Lean forward as far as you can without rounding your back. The bar doesn't have to touch the floor.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. Straps are fine if your grip gives out first.

exercises.name: Rope straight-arm pulldown
cues: Attach a rope to the high pulley and grip the ends, palms facing each other.
Stable stance, knees slightly bent, torso leaning slightly forward; core braced, a slight bend in the elbows.
Pull the rope down by moving your arms along your sides until your hands reach your hips; don't bend the elbows more.
Return under control.
exercises.safety: Keep the shoulders down; the elbow angle stays the same throughout.

exercises.name: Russian twist
cues: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor or slightly lifted.
Hold a weight plate (or a medicine ball or kettlebell) with both hands in front of your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back and your core braced.
Rotate your torso to bring the weight toward one hip while your hips stay still. Return to the middle and rotate to the other side; do the same number each way.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight and your hips still; it can be done with no weight to start. The photos hook the feet under a bench; the reference keeps them on the floor or slightly lifted.

exercises.name: Seal row (cambered bar)
cues: Lie on your stomach on a bench with the bar on the floor below you.
Grip it overhand, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Breathe in and pull the bar as high as you can, ideally to the underside of the bench.
Lower it with control.
exercises.safety: The bench supports your chest, so your lower back rests. The photos use a cambered bar, which lets it travel higher on a low bench.

exercises.name: Seated barbell shoulder press
cues: Use an upright shoulder-press bench in a rack with the bar at about shoulder height when seated.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, unrack, and lean back against the pad.
Lower the bar with control, in front of your face, back to your shoulders.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Keep the bar in front of your head, not behind the neck. A spotter makes the unrack easier.

exercises.name: Seated bent-over reverse fly
cues: Sit on the end of a bench and lean forward with a straight back, dumbbells hanging toward the floor.
With your elbows slightly bent and fixed, raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are about level with your body.
Lower them back slowly.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and no swinging; don't shrug. The reference describes it standing bent over; seated, the arms move the same way.

exercises.name: Seated calf raise
cues: Sit with the knee pad snug on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform.
Release the lever and lower your heels slowly to a full stretch.
Push up onto your toes as high as you can and pause.
exercises.safety: Get a full stretch at the bottom and a full contraction at the top of each rep; no bouncing or short, choppy reps.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell curl
cues: Sit on the end of a flat bench, a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, palms facing forward, elbows close to your body.
Curl the dumbbells up with control by bending your elbows.
Lower them back to the start.
exercises.safety: The reference describes the standing curl; seated, the arms move the same way. Keep your elbows from drifting forward or back, and keep your wrists straight. If you start to swing, use less weight.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Sit on the end of a flat bench, feet flat, dumbbells hanging at your sides on almost straight arms.
With control, lift the dumbbells out to your sides until your upper arms are horizontal; no higher.
Lower them with control. Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout.
exercises.safety: It's easy to go too heavy on raises: pick a weight you can lift with strict form and no swinging. Don't arch your back or roll your shoulders forward. The reference describes it standing; seated, the arms move the same way.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Sit on a bench with the back raised upright, feet flat, back against the pad.
Bring the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms forward; brace your core and keep your chest up.
Press up to straight arms over your shoulders without slamming the elbows locked.
Lower under control back to your shoulders. No bouncing at the bottom.
exercises.safety: Keep your back pressed against the backrest; arching hard puts stress on your spine.

exercises.name: Seated one-arm wrist curl
cues: Sit and rest one forearm on your thigh, palm up, wrist just past your knee, dumbbell in hand.
Lower your hand toward the floor and let the dumbbell roll out into your fingers.
Close your grip and bend your wrist up. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and a slow, full range. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: Seated one-arm wrist extension
cues: Sit and rest one forearm on your thigh, palm down, wrist just past your knee, dumbbell in hand.
Lower your hand toward the floor.
Bend your wrist upward. Finish the reps, then switch arms.
exercises.safety: Use a light weight and slow, full reps. One set = both arms.

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
cues: Lie on your back, one foot flat with the knee bent, the other leg extended.
Tuck your pelvis slightly.
Push your hips up with the bent leg until your body is straight; squeeze at the top.
Lower and repeat. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Hips stay level; don't let the free side drop. Add a weight on your hips when it gets easy.

exercises.name: Single-leg kettlebell deadlift
cues: Stand on one leg, slight bend in the knee, kettlebell in the opposite hand.
Hinge forward at the hip while your free leg extends straight back, body moving as one line.
Lower the kettlebell toward the floor without touching it, back flat, hips square.
Drive through the standing heel to return upright. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Balance is the limit at first: start light, and touch a rack with your free hand if you wobble. One set = both legs.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Single leg deadlift with kettlebell

exercises.name: Sit-up
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent to about 90°, feet hooked under something that won't move.
Hands in front of your chest (the reference's position; the photos show hands behind the head).
Lift your upper body by contracting your abs and bend forward as far as you can.
Return to the starting position.
exercises.safety: Hold a weight against your chest to make it harder.

exercises.name: Smith machine bench press
