cues: Set the bench so the bar comes down over your lower chest. Shoulder blades back and down, chest up.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, unrack by rotating the bar off the hooks.
Lower with control until the bar touches your chest.
Press straight up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Set the machine's stoppers just below chest height. Re-hook the bar by rotating your wrists at the top.

exercises.name: Smith machine bent-over row
cues: Set the bar just below knee height. Feet about shoulder-width, grip overhand slightly wider than your shoulders.
Push your hips back and lean forward, back neither rounded nor arched, arms straight.
Unhook the bar and pull it to your lower chest or upper abs, shoulder blades together.
Lower with control.
exercises.safety: Your lower back holds the position the whole set. The reference covers the free-barbell row; the rails only guide the bar.

exercises.name: Smith machine Bulgarian split squat
cues: Set the bar at shoulder height and put a knee-high bench about one long step behind where you will stand.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back and rest the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Squat down with control until your back knee is just off the floor.
Push through your front foot to stand back up. Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: Let your front knee track in the direction of your toes. Balance is the limit at first: start light. One set = both legs.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Smith machine Bulgarian split squat

exercises.name: Smith machine calf raise
cues: Put a plate or block under the bar and set the bar at shoulder height.
Stand on the block with the balls of your feet, heels hanging off, bar on your upper back; unrack it.
Lower your heels to a full stretch, then rise as high as you can with straight knees.
exercises.safety: Get a full stretch at the bottom and a full contraction at the top of each rep; no bouncing or short, choppy reps. The reference uses a free barbell; the Smith rails only guide the bar.

exercises.name: Smith machine close-grip bench press
cues: Put a flat bench under the Smith bar. Lie down, shoulder blades together and down.
Grip narrower than a regular bench press, hands about directly above your shoulders, and unhook the bar.
Lower with control until the bar touches your chest around where the ribs end.
Press back up.
exercises.safety: Set the stoppers just below your chest. Expect to use less weight than your regular bench. The reference covers the free-barbell version; the rails only guide the bar.

exercises.name: Smith machine incline press
cues: Set an incline bench (about 30–45°) so the bar comes down to your upper chest. Shoulder blades back and down.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and rotate the bar off the hooks.
Lower with control until the bar touches your upper chest.
Press straight up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Set the stoppers just above where the bar touches your chest.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Smith machine incline bench press

exercises.name: Smith machine Romanian deadlift
cues: Set the bar at mid-thigh height. Feet shoulder-width, overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Unrack standing tall, brace, back flat.
Push your hips back and lower the bar along the front of your legs, knees slightly bent, until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. Set the stoppers just below your lowest point.

exercises.name: Smith machine shoulder press
cues: Put a bench with an upright back under the bar so the bar comes down in front of your face.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders, rotate the bar off the hooks.
Lower with control to your upper chest (about chin height or a little below).
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Set the stoppers just above where the bar touches your chest. Bar in front of the face, never behind the neck.

refs.title: StrengthLog: Seated Smith machine shoulder press

exercises.name: Smith machine squat
cues: Bar on your upper back, feet about shoulder-width, directly under the bar or a little in front of it.
Brace, breathe in and rotate the bar off the hooks.
Squat as deep as you can with good form.
Stand back up and re-hook the bar at the top.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique. Set the stoppers just below your lowest point: you can't tip a Smith bar off to the side if you get stuck.

exercises.name: Smith machine upright row
cues: Set the bar at about mid-thigh height. Grip it overhand, hands slightly narrower than shoulder-width, and unrack.
Pull the bar straight up toward your chin, close to your body, elbows out to the sides.
Stop before your upper arms go above shoulder height.
Lower the bar with control.
exercises.safety: The reference covers the free-barbell upright row; the rails only guide the bar. Same rules: light weights, few sets, and reverse earlier if your shoulders hurt.

exercises.name: Spider curl
cues: Lie with your chest and stomach on a 45° bench, a dumbbell in each hand, underhand grip, upper arms hanging vertical.
Curl the dumbbells up with control.
Don't let your upper arms move back or forward.
Lower back to the start, keeping tension at the bottom.
exercises.safety: Expect to use light dumbbells.

exercises.name: Stability ball crunch
cues: Sit on the ball and walk your feet out until your shoulders, back and tailbone rest on it; feet hip-width, knees at 90°.
Hands behind your head, elbows back; keep them there throughout.
Tuck your chin slightly and curl your ribs toward your hips until your upper back lifts off the ball; hold briefly.
Lower slowly back onto the ball. Your lower back and tailbone stay on the ball the whole time.
exercises.safety: Don't arch your lower back or pull on your head. The second photo leans further back than ACE's start position: stop with your back resting along the ball. Widen your feet if balance is hard.

exercises.name: Stability ball knee tuck
cues: Lie face down over the ball, hands and feet on the floor. Walk your hands forward until your shins rest on the ball, hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line.
Brace and pull your knees toward your chest, rolling the ball forward until your knees are under your hips; hold briefly.
Push your legs back out to the straight-line start.
exercises.safety: Don't let your lower back sag or your hips hike up at the start. ACE rates it advanced: master the plank first.

exercises.name: Stability-ball leg curl
cues: Lie on your back, arms at your sides, heels on an exercise ball, legs straight.
Brace and lift your hips so your body is straight from feet to shoulders.
Bend your knees to roll the ball toward you, keeping your hips up.
Slowly straighten your legs to roll it back.
exercises.safety: Keep your hips lifted the whole set. Make sure the ball is properly inflated.

exercises.name: Standing (kneeling) leg curl
cues: Set the machine so the pad sits just above the heel of the working leg; hold the handles.
Keep your upper body still.
Curl your heel toward your glutes, pause briefly, then lower slowly.
Finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.safety: No swinging. One set = both legs.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your shoulders.
Breathe in and lightly brace your core.
Press the dumbbells up to straight arms.
Lower them with control back to your shoulders.
exercises.safety: No leg drive or leaning back. Pressing one arm at a time works the obliques more.

exercises.name: Stiff-legged deadlift
cues: Feet shoulder-width or narrower, overhand grip, knees only slightly bent and staying that way.
Hinge at the hips, lowering the bar close to your legs, back straight.
Go down until you feel a strong hamstring stretch (the bar can touch the floor between reps if you can keep your back flat).
Stand back up by driving your hips forward.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. Needs good hamstring flexibility; start with the bar on low blocks if you can't reach the floor with a flat back.

exercises.name: Straight-arm pulldown
cues: Set the pulley high. Grip the bar overhand, a bit wider than your shoulders, and step back.
Lean forward slightly, knees soft, arms straight out in front.
Keeping your arms straight, sweep the bar down to your thighs.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are about level with your head.
exercises.safety: Elbows stay almost straight the whole time; bending them turns it into a pushdown.

exercises.name: Sumo (plié) dumbbell squat
cues: Wide stance, toes pointed out; hold one dumbbell by the top plate between your legs.
Brace, chest up, and lower straight down between your legs as far as your hips allow.
Heels stay down and knees track over your toes.
Push through your whole foot to stand.
exercises.safety: Needs good hip mobility; only go as wide and as deep as is comfortable.

exercises.name: Sumo barbell squat
cues: Set the bar in a rack at about sternum height, bar on your upper back; unrack and step back.
Take a wide stance with your feet pointing slightly out. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Bend your knees and hips together to lower straight down between your legs, as far as your mobility allows with your heels on the floor.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.
exercises.safety: Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes. Go as deep as you can with good technique. Always set the safety arms just below your lowest point. Needs good hip mobility; only go as wide as is comfortable.

exercises.name: Sumo deadlift
cues: Wide stance, toes turned out, bar over the middle of your feet, shins vertical when viewed from the front.
Grip the bar inside your legs, arms straight. Breathe in and brace.
Push your knees out and the floor away, pulling the bar close to your body until you stand tall.
Lower under control and reset your breath.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. A little easier on the lower back than the conventional deadlift. Experiment with stance width.

exercises.name: Suspended knee tuck
cues: Set suspension straps with the foot cradles about a foot off the floor. Put both feet in them and get into a push-up position directly under the anchor, hands under your shoulders.
Brace, keep your feet together and your body straight.
Draw your knees toward your chest until they are under your hips, letting your hips rise and spine curl.
Slowly extend back to the push-up position.
exercises.safety: Don't let your lower back sag, and don't swing the straps. The second photo lifts the hips higher than the reference: stop with your knees under your hips. ACE rates it advanced.

exercises.name: T-bar row
cues: Straddle the bar (or stand on the machine's platform) and grip the handle.
Hips back, back flat, arms straight.
Pull the handle toward your chest as high as you can, shoulder blades squeezing together.
Lower with control to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Like the barbell row, your lower back holds the position: keep it flat and stop if you start heaving with your hips.

exercises.name: Tate press
cues: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells held straight up over your chest, palms facing your feet.
Bend your elbows out to the sides and lower the dumbbells until they nearly touch your chest.
Extend your elbows to press them back up.
exercises.safety: Light dumbbells and slow reps; the flared-elbow path is unusual, so stop if the elbows or shoulders complain.

exercises.name: Trap bar deadlift
cues: Stand inside the bar with the handles in line with the middle of your feet.
Breathe in, bend down and grip the handles; chest up, back flat.
Brace and stand up until you're tall, pushing the floor away.
Lower under control and reset your breath.
exercises.safety: Keep your back straight (neutral), never rounded; if it rounds, lower the weight. Apart from normal muscle soreness this shouldn't hurt your back: aches mean too much, too soon, so cut the volume and check your form. The high handles shorten the range if you can't reach the low ones with a flat back.

exercises.name: Triceps pushdown (bar)
cues: Face a high pulley with a short bar, overhand grip, feet shoulder-width, core braced.
Start with the bar at upper-chest level, elbows bent and tucked at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Let it rise under control; only the elbows move.
exercises.safety: Don't lean over the bar or arch your back to move it; use a weight you control.

exercises.name: Triceps pushdown (rope)
cues: Rope on a high pulley, overhand grip, one step back, core braced.
Upper arms vertical and tucked at your sides.
Push down until your arms are fully extended.
Let it rise under control.
exercises.safety: Only the elbows move; avoid momentum. Heavy weight with low reps feels uncomfortable in the elbows for many people.

exercises.name: Triceps pushdown (V-bar)
cues: V-bar on a high pulley, overhand grip, feet shoulder-width, core braced.
Elbows bent and tucked at your sides.
Push down to fully straight arms.
Let it rise under control.
exercises.safety: Keep your upper arms and body still.

exercises.name: Two-arm kettlebell row
cues: Stand with your feet about hip-width, two kettlebells in front of your feet.
Hinge forward at the hips with a neutral spine, brace your core and grab the kettlebells.
Pull them toward you as far as you can, elbows close to your sides, shoulder blades pulled back.
Lower with control and start the next rep before they touch the floor.
exercises.safety: No swinging with your upper body; your lower back holds the bent-over position.

exercises.name: Underhand lat pulldown
cues: Grip the bar with palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart. Thighs under the pad.
Chest up, eyes on the bar.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, elbows down toward your sides.
Return slowly to straight arms.
exercises.safety: Keep the reps smooth; leaning far back turns it into a row.

exercises.name: Walking lunge (bodyweight)
cues: Stand tall, hands on hips, with clear floor space ahead.
Step forward into a lunge, back knee just above the floor.
Push up and step through into the next lunge with the other leg.
exercises.safety: Hold dumbbells once 20 reps per leg is easy.

exercises.name: Wrist roller
cues: Stand with feet shoulder-width, holding the roller in both hands, arms straight out in front of you, weight hanging on the cord.
Roll the bar forward with your wrists, winding the cord until the weight reaches the bar.
Slowly reverse the motion to lower the weight back down. One rep = all the way up and down.
exercises.safety: Lower slowly by unwinding; don't let the weight drop.

exercises.name: Zercher squat
cues: Set the bar in a rack at about elbow height. Rest it in the crooks of your elbows, elbows close together.
Back out of the rack and brace your core.
Squat down as in a regular squat, as deep as you can with your back straight, pulling the bar into your body.
Stand back up through your heels.
exercises.safety: It's rough on the elbow crooks at first: start light and wrap a towel around the bar if it hurts. Don't round your back. Set the safety arms.

exercises.name: Zottman curl
cues: Curl the dumbbells up with palms facing up.
At the top, turn your palms to face down.
Lower slowly with palms down, then turn them back up at the bottom.
exercises.safety: Pick a weight you can lower slowly palms-down; that's the weak part of the rep.
